component: P16 direct comparison and measurement probe recheck
constraints: Offline observation of actual Python verifier return objects and interpreter-traced allocations, with an independent Node Ed25519/hash primitive check.
Six primitive cases, five lexical rejections, one batch of 128 admissions. Parent bounds input at 64 KiB and counts each output stream against 4 KiB; no target-class latency or memory SLA.
alternatives: Python asyncio subprocess protocol and a Node native-crypto primitive observer.
Julia BenchmarkTools trials with configurable samples, evaluations and timing budget.
C#/F#/VB BenchmarkDotNet runtime jobs and statistical summaries.
Dedicated foreign-process supervision with an explicit Python observation/report boundary.
rationale: KEEP the Python observer: actual return types and Python traced allocations are the required observables. A foreign harness still needs this boundary; independently reimplementing the verifier would change the experiment.
KEEP the Node primitive check: documented native crypto verifies the same fixed messages and hash input through a separate runtime. It is explicitly not full passport admission parity.

BenchmarkTools and BenchmarkDotNet materially improve statistical experiment design when that is required. This probe intentionally emits single-batch diagnostics and denies runtime ranking, jitter and worst-case bounds. A framework migration does not strengthen the stated object/capture checks; no performance winner is inferred.

Nineteen current focused methods pass without skips, including real subprocess overflow/exit/timeout, response types, integer intervals, tracing ownership and changed-source rejection. A fresh live run confirms six primitive cases and five lexical rejections. No new mismatch was demonstrated.
limits: These are trusted developer diagnostics, not deployed command, sensor, transport or authority services. No hardware, hard-real-time, MLS/CNSA, availability or complete-phase qualification.
Five listed files per tool are compared before/after execution. This is not an atomic snapshot, loaded-code attestation or dependency closure and misses transient restoration.
Alternatives were researched from official sources, not executed or benchmarked. KEEP is not based on installation, familiarity or rewrite cost.
Exchange timeout excludes OS process creation and has separate cooperative cleanup. Direct-child termination does not manage descendants; retained bytes are not total RSS or kernel/transient buffers.
Node stdin is read as a trusted parent-generated input; the subsequent size assertion is not hostile-stream admission. Local timing samples include scheduling effects and loop overhead.
